It is all published, in technical Japanese. Reading it takes two skills at once: the language and the field.

*How many decisions do you make without seeing what is taking shape in your sector in Japan?*

**You enter Japan with a global price list. It says nothing about the market you are entering.**

Set low out of caution, the entry price becomes the reference and never rises again. Each distribution tier then takes its margin, and the end customer pays a price you did not choose. Correcting it means knowing how a price increase is won in Japan, after thirty years of deflation.

*Were your Japanese prices built, or inherited from elsewhere?*

## Who is this for?

**European industrial companies and mid-caps that have to decide about Japan** without being able to read the data behind the decision. Strategy, innovation and R&D teams: automotive, aerospace and defence, energy, advanced materials.

The trigger is almost always the same. A Japanese player moves, a market opens, and nothing available in English settles the question.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## My approach

I go back to the data itself: patents, transactions, sales. I extract it, structure it, and interpret it in its sector context.

What remains is knowing what it proves. Causal inference and Bayesian modelling separate what causes a result from what merely accompanies it, and put a number on the uncertainty that is left. You will know what you can assert, and what still needs checking.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

library(ggplot2)
set.seed(69)
n <- 60
rain <- rbeta(n, 2, 5) * 100
umbrellas <- 200 + 8 * rain + rnorm(n, sd = 50)
coffees <- 1000 + 15 * rain + rnorm(n, sd = 100)
data <- data.frame(umbrellas = umbrellas, coffees = coffees, rain = rain)

ggplot(data, aes(x = umbrellas, y = coffees)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = rain), size = 4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#e63946", linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#f4a261", high = "#457b9d", name = "Rainy days (%)") +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation ≠ Causation",
    subtitle = "Umbrella sales correlate with coffee consumption.\nShould you distribute umbrellas to sell more coffee?",
    x = "Umbrella sales",
    y = "Coffees consumed",
    caption = "The real cause: the weather. My work: identifying these hidden variables in your data."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 13, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.2),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "gray50", face = "italic", size = 11),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
